entities.name: Leukon II of Bosporus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Leucon II of Bosporus, also known as Leuco, was a Spartocid ruler of the Bosporan Kingdom in 240 BC.

He succeeded his half-brother Scaetes I after Paerisades II's death, taking control of the kingdom at around 230 BC. This marked the beginning of a period of instability and power struggles within the Bosporan monarchy.

Leucon II is notable for being one of the few rulers of the Bosporan Kingdom to be mentioned in ancient Greek sources, such as those by the historian Polybius.
